items.title: Reconcile the ledger’s version, then publish to @flashynetwork once named
items.detail: Correction: this item was filed on a stale, shallow clone of this repository that predated commit c00c482c (2026-10-26, "Rename the package to @flashyos/ledger, version 1.0.1"). That commit already did exactly what this item asked for, for a better-documented reason than I had: the GitHub org rename (FlashyLabs -> AgenteLabs) broke @flashylabs’s GitHub Packages scope resolution outright, so ClaimYour.Gold’s npm ci started 404ing on @flashylabs/ledger@0.8.0. The fix published @flashyos/ledger 1.0.1 to PUBLIC npm (not GitHub Packages) and updated this repo’s own package.json, .npmrc (removed) and publish.yml to match; ClaimYour.Gold’s dependency is confirmed updated to "@flashyos/ledger": "^1.0.1" on its own main. All three numbers this item worried about now agree. It was not an out-of-band hand-publish — it was a committed, reasoned CI change I simply hadn’t read before filing this. The one thing still genuinely open is the later move from @flashyos/ledger to @flashynetwork/ledger once that scope is actually used for something — tracked in flashyos’s own backlog item on the @flashynetwork decision, not here.
